paper.title_en: Primordial black holes in braneworld gravity: A gateway to hidden dimensions and the dark Universe
paper.abstract_en: This thesis investigates the cosmological dynamics of primordial black holes (PBHs) within the Randall--Sundrum Type II braneworld scenario. The work comprises a preliminary discussion on gravitational collapse in the small-black-hole limit at early cosmological epochs, and two principal studies. The first study presents a fully relativistic treatment of PBH accretion in the early Universe, employing Michel accretion theory within the covariant Shiromizu--Maeda--Sasaki formalism. The analysis reveals that higher-dimensional effects substantially enhance early-time accretion onto light PBHs, with discrepancies between our black hole masses and previous estimates growing with cosmic time as $t^{0.33}$--- a difference that reaches several orders of magnitude by the end of the strong-accretion epoch. This finding fundamentally alters the mapping between the initial PBH mass spectrum and present-day populations. The second study reassesses the observational and cosmological constraints on higher-dimensional PBHs in Randall--Sundrum cosmologies. Constraints from direct Hawking radiation, unresolved diffuse gamma-ray backgrounds, microlensing surveys, and energy injection into the cosmic microwave background are reanalysed in light of the modified higher-dimensional evaporation dynamics and updated observational surveys. Taken together, these results identify viable regions of parameter space in which PBHs can account for the entirety of dark matter while remaining consistent with current observational bounds. Notably, due to the enhanced accretion epoch, PBHs capable of constituting a significant fraction of dark matter may originate from masses below the effective four-dimensional Planck scale. This thesis thus puts forward a dark matter candidate with a distinct evolutionary history and observational signatures today.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 该论文在Randall-Sundrum II膜世界引力框架下系统研究原初黑洞的吸积与蒸发，涉及霍金辐射、高维蒸发动力学与暗物质约束，理论上较深入且对原初黑洞质量谱与暗物质候选给出可检验预言；摘要结构清晰、方法明确，虽为学位论文且尚无引用，仍值得点击进一步阅读。
decision.title_zh: 膜世界引力中的原初黑洞：通往隐藏维度与暗宇宙的门户
decision.abstract_zh: 本论文研究Randall--Sundrum II型膜世界场景中原初黑洞（PBHs）的宇宙学动力学。工作包括对早期宇宙学时期小黑洞极限下引力坍缩的初步讨论，以及两项主要研究。第一项研究给出早期宇宙中原初黑洞吸积的完全相对论性处理，在协变Shiromizu--Maeda--Sasaki形式体系中采用Michel吸积理论。分析表明，高维效应显著增强轻原初黑洞在早期时刻的吸积，我们得到的黑洞质量与先前估计之间的差异随宇宙时间以$t^{0.33}$增长——到强吸积纪元结束时该差异可达若干数量级。这一发现从根本上改变了初始原初黑洞质量谱与当今种群之间的映射。第二项研究在Randall--Sundrum宇宙学中重新评估对高维原初黑洞的观测与宇宙学约束。来自直接霍金辐射、未分辨弥散伽马射线背景、微引力透镜巡天以及向宇宙微波背景能量注入的约束，在修正的高维蒸发动力学和更新观测巡天的基础上被重新分析。综合来看，这些结果确定了参数空间中的可行区域，在其中原初黑洞可以解释全部暗物质，同时与当前观测界限保持一致。值得注意的是，由于增强的吸积纪元，能够构成暗物质显著份额的原初黑洞可能起源于低于有效四维普朗克尺度的质量。因此，本论文提出了一个具有独特演化历史和当今观测特征的暗物质候选者。
